cards.explanation: The answer is Assyria, friends. God says, “Look at Assyria, a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches that shaded the forest.” So the first tree in this message is a whole nation dressed up as a cedar. I think Pharaoh is being told to take a good, long look.

The answer is the waters and deep springs. Water, water, WATER! God says, “The waters made it grow; the deep springs made it tall…” Those springs sent their streams all around its base. This tree had a serious water supply, and it grew like it knew it.
The answer is shade, friends! The text says, “all the great nations lived in its shade.” Think of a tree so big that whole nations set up under it. That's a lot of folks sharing one patch of cool.

The answer is False. God says, “The cedars in the garden of God could not rival it…” The cypresses couldn't compare with its branches, and the plane trees couldn't match its boughs. This tree had no competition.

The answer is True, friends! God says, “I made it beautiful with its many branches…” So the beauty didn't start with the tree. God is the one who says He made it beautiful. Hold onto that, because it matters for what's coming.

The answer is that it grew proud of its height. God says the cedar “…grew proud on account of its height…” After all those verses of praise, this is the line that turns the whole message. Beautiful branches were never the problem, and the text puts the pride right next to the height.
The answer is False. The text says, “And all the peoples of the earth left its shade and abandoned it.” Remember how the great nations lived in that shade earlier? Now they're gone.
The answer is on its fallen trunk, friends. The text says, “All the birds of the air nested on its fallen trunk…” The tree is lying down now. That's a big change from the high branches.

The answer is False. God says, “This happened so that no other trees by the waters would become great in height and set their tops among the clouds…” The other trees aren't meant to follow that path. This is a heavy part, so I'll let the words stand.

The answer is that they faint because of it. The text says, “…all the trees of the field fainted because of it.” God also says He made Lebanon mourn for it. The trees of the field are reacting to the fall.
The answer is quake, friends. God says, “I made the nations quake at the sound of its downfall…” The sound of the downfall is what sets them quaking. God is the One who made it happen.

The answer is its allies among the nations, friends! The text says, “As its allies they had lived in its shade among the nations.” So these trees were its allies, living under the same big branches. They went down with it.

The answer is True. God says to Pharaoh, “You also will be brought down to the depths of the earth to be with the trees of Eden.” The message started with Pharaoh's greatness and ends with Pharaoh himself. The text says it plainly.
